correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction of the Alikhanov interpolants gives W22=A/epsilon+o(1/epsilon), W32=B/epsilon+o(1/epsilon), and W33=O(1), with A=alpha/((1-alpha)(2-alpha))>0 and B>0 by kernel pairing. The fixed increments q=-B/(2A),1 yield epsilon*Gamma(1-alpha)*energy -> -B^2/(4A). The standard-library exact-panel checker provides an explicit negative rational-mesh integer-increment example at alpha=1/2; separately implemented exact formulas verify three fractional-order samples numerically. Finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Nonuniform Alikhanov energy coercivity underlies published stability theory for adaptive fractional subdiffusion. This all-order three-increment collapse exhibits a specific unavoidable obstruction to unrestricted-mesh positivity and a quantified inverse-middle-step blow-up. It distinguishes a substantive sign failure from mere nonapplicability of sufficient conditions and guides mesh-ratio safeguards. It does not assert numerical-solution instability or sharpen a published positive ratio threshold.
